title: Meet Sauvignon Blanc
subtitle: Green, zesty and aromatic
objectives: Describe Sauvignon Blanc's flavours and structure

steps.title: Pungent and fresh
steps.body: Sauvignon Blanc gives crisp, aromatic whites with gooseberry, lime, grapefruit, passion fruit, cut grass, green pepper, elderflower and sometimes a flinty or smoky note. Acidity is high, body light to medium. Most is unoaked and drunk young. It's one of the most recognisable white grapes.

steps.title: Origins
steps.body: Sauvignon Blanc probably comes from the Loire or Bordeaux; its name may come from sauvage, wild, for its vigorous growth. DNA shows a close link to Savagnin, of the Traminer family. Crossed with Cabernet Franc, it gave Cabernet Sauvignon in 17th century Bordeaux. It buds late and ripens early.

steps.prompt: Which famous red grape is Sauvignon Blanc a parent of?
steps.explanation: Sauvignon Blanc crossed with Cabernet Franc gave Cabernet Sauvignon.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for pale lemon-green colour, an intense nose of gooseberry, grass and citrus, sometimes tropical fruit, and a crisp, mouth-watering palate. Compared with Riesling, it's more green and herbal, less floral; compared with Chardonnay, much more aromatic and usually unoaked.

steps.prompt: Most Sauvignon Blanc is aged in new oak.
steps.explanation: Not true. Most is unoaked, to keep its fresh aromas.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sauvignon Blanc gives gooseberry, grass and citrus
It's a parent of Cabernet Sauvignon
It's crisp, aromatic and usually unoaked
